Peter, I’m writing to you today with gratitude and a renewed sense of urgency. First, thank you. Because of you, we just hit our February end-of-month fundraising goal. Your sustained support proves a powerful truth: **we can take Republicans on, and we can win.** Just look at what we’ve already accomplished together. The historic victories of Senators Jon Ossoff and Reverend Raphael Warnock are a testament to what’s possible when Georgians unite in the name of progress. And just last year, Georgians across the state voted for change in special elections — rejecting chaos and sending a clear message that Georgia wants leaders who defend our democracy — **not attack it.** But the fight is far from over. The right to vote in Georgia is still under a coordinated, relentless assault. Last week was huge. Can we make this week even bigger?
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260302-2570)
Peter,
I have to stop and say thank you.
Last week, 647 individual donations came in from all across Wisconsin. It was our biggest grassroots fundraising week of 2026. This level of support doesn't happen unless people really believe in what we're building.
Last week's first-place finish in the Marquette poll confirmed what this movement has known for some time: Wisconsin is ready for change. We've been leading the way on the issues that matter — affordable childcare, fully funded schools, reining in unchecked AI data center construction and protecting families from utility hikes — and people are paying attention. The numbers are catching up to the movement we’ve all been building.
The other campaigns are watching these numbers too. They see a grassroots candidate gaining ground, and they are going to come at us with everything they've got. March is a critical month. Matching last week isn’t enough — we need to grow from it.
There’s no PAC money waiting in the wings, no corporate donors writing big checks. There’s just people chipping in whatever they can — $5, $10, $50 — because they believe Wisconsin deserves better.
[**If you haven't yet, the single most impactful thing you can do right now is set up a small monthly donation.**](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260227.6UkJkJ&refcode=em20260302-2570&t=1&akid=2570%2E105371%2EBdnyId)
[**Even $5 a month adds up fast when thousands of people do it together.**](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260227.6UkJkJ&refcode=em20260302-2570&t=2&akid=2570%2E105371%2EBdnyId)
We're building something real here. Thank you for being part of it.
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260227.6UkJkJ&amount=5&refcode=em20260302-2570&t=21&akid=2570%2E105371%2EBdnyId)**
With gratitude,
— Fran and team
[**P.S. — If you're already a monthly donor, thank you! You are the backbone of this campaign. If you're able to increase your gift by even $1, it makes a bigger difference than you'd think.**](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260227.6UkJkJ&refcode=em20260302-2570&t=22&akid=2570%2E105371%2EBdnyId)
**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_fh_footer?refcode=em20260302-2570&t=23&refcode2=2570_105371_BdnyId&akid=2570%2E105371%2EBdnyId)**

The more people who engage with our emails, the more likely we’ll go straight to your inbox. For a free and easy way to help our campaign, please [click this link to our website](https://francescahong.com/) after you finish reading our emails.

Wages just aren’t keeping up with rising costs for housing, childcare, and groceries — and hard-working people are stretched far too thin. I've spent my career delivering for working families: writing the Affordable Care Act and then defending it as California Attorney General, getting vaccines to folks as HHS Secretary when it mattered most during the pandemic, and negotiating lower prescription prices for seniors. body:
https://rokhanna.com [https://rokhanna.com]
Peter,
Today, I stood with Senator Bernie Sanders to propose a bold federal Billionaire Tax.
Here’s what it does:
It raises an estimated $4.5 trillion by asking the ultra-wealthy to finally pay their fair share.
And it uses that money to:
* Expand Medicare to cover dental, vision, and hearing
* Strengthen and extend healthcare access
* Provide a $3,000 check to every American earning under $150,000
* Guarantee a $60,000 minimum salary for every public school teacher.
At a time when working families are being squeezed by rising costs, and Republicans are pouring trillions into tax breaks and bloated Pentagon budgets, we’re saying something simple:
In the richest country on Earth, no senior should go without dental care. No family should skip hearing aids because of cost. And working Americans deserve direct relief.
For too long, billionaires have paid lower effective tax rates than teachers, nurses, and firefighters.
That ends now.
Bernie and I are building a movement to pass this bill, but we need you with us.
Will you sign your name to support the Sanders-Khanna Billionaire Tax and demand Congress put working people first? body:
Hi Peter, I'm writing this after breaking my fast.
Tonight’s iftar was simple, and I forgot to take a picture. But one night last week, I broke my fast with this waffle from Saj Bakery Canton — and yes, it was as good as it looks:
[](https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260302-1-ak.dfGO6g&amount=5&refcode=em20260302-1747&t=2&akid=1782%2E251025%2EuaYXsf)
During Ramadan, from sunrise to sunset, we don’t eat or drink. Not even water.
By mid-afternoon, you definitely feel it. It’s hard, but just because something is hard doesn’t mean it isn’t worth doing.
Fasting isn’t about deprivation. It’s about discipline. Clarity. Remembering who you are and what you stand for.
This campaign has felt a little like that.
We could take the easy route — call a couple of billionaires, open the door to corporate PACs, and make a few quiet deals in exchange for large checks.
However, doing so would cost us our independence. **And I won’t run a campaign funded by the same forces that rigged this system.**
That’s why from day one, I’ve never taken corporate PAC money, and I never will.
Ramadan teaches patience. It teaches intention. It teaches that restraint today builds strength tomorrow.
That’s what we’re trying to build here — a campaign rooted in values, not shortcuts. But I won’t lie to you, this is the harder route.
Running a campaign like this means I have to constantly be asking everyday folks for $25, $10, or even $5.
I don’t love asking, but it’s the only way to build something that answers to working people instead of corporate donors. If you’re able tonight, will you chip in a few bucks to help us keep building this campaign the right way?
[**https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-ms-aes-20260302-1-ak**](https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260302-1-ak.dfGO6g&amount=5&refcode=em20260302-1747&t=3&akid=1782%2E251025%2EuaYXsf)
Thank you,
Abdul

name: Tim Kaine
subject: Trump’s illegal war in Iran
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Kaine for Virginia
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cgp-2026 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cgp-2026]
Friends,
The news that the United States has joined Israel in starting an offensive war against Iran while in the middle of diplomatic negotiations is tragic and deeply alarming.
As a member of the Senate Armed Services and Foreign Relations Committees, with access to classified information about threats from Iran and others, I can say plainly that there was no imminent threat to the United States.
Not a single one that justified sending our sons and daughters into another Middle East war — especially without the public debate and vote that the Constitution requires from Congress before any declaration of war.
That’s why I’m insisting the Senate immediately return to session and vote on my War Powers Resolution to stop illegal U.S. hostilities against Iran.
Congress cannot remain silent while a president wages war without authorization, and every single Senator needs to go on the record about this dangerous, unnecessary, and frankly idiotic action.
More war is not the answer. If it were, the last 70 years would have produced a better outcome than what we see today.
President Trump tore up a working diplomatic agreement that prevented Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons.

name: Adam Schiff
subject: our oversight work is just beginning
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY SCHIFF FOR SENATE
body:
[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/62?t=1001&akid=9592%2E5257348%2EYijGb8 ]Adam Schiff for Senate

Hi Derek,

I want to tell you about the work I’m doing to bring oversight and
accountability to the Trump administration and major corporations bending
the knee.

I hope you come away from this email recognizing that, while things often
feel so bleak these days, there is important work being done to create
some order, some accountability, and some decency in Washington.

Derek, when I was
first elected to the Senate, I was determined to do things a little
differently and bring some of my oversight work to the upper chamber.

And under the second Trump administration, there’s been plenty of work to
do. Oftentimes, in such a target-rich environment, it’s difficult to know
where to begin.

For example, investigating the ICE detention centers across California and
beyond, where Trump and his administration have been cruelly rounding up
immigrants, many of whom are here legally.

[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/5891?t=1004&akid=9592%2E5257348%2EYijGb8 ]California US Senators Alex Padilla, Adam Schiff conduct oversight of
Kern County ICE detention center

We have all watched in horror as ICE has engaged in indiscriminate
immigration raids, grabbing citizens and noncitizens alike, and often
endangering the lives of our neighbors in the process.

That’s why I joined Alex Padilla in conducting oversight of what is
happening when a friend, neighbor, or family member is detained by ICE.

What we heard — and exposed — was shocking. Detainees who never committed
a crime, held in prison conditions, with limited access to family, lawyers
and most seriously, needed medical care.

Derek, I have
also led oversight on Trump’s latest pay-to-play arrangement, where he
offers million-dollar donors special access to the White House, all under
the guise of celebrating America’s 250th birthday.

[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/5891?t=1005&akid=9592%2E5257348%2EYijGb8 ]Sen. Schiff leads probe into Freedom250, the America birthday group
offering access to Trump for donations

This investigation pissed off Trump officials — a White House spokesman
said, “It’s a complete disgrace that Pencil-Neck Adam Schiff is willing to
trash the United States of America during its semiquincentennial
celebration simply because he hates President Trump.”

To that, I can’t help but sigh. Another insult from a high-ranking
official, simply for doing my job. And exposing this utter grift cloaked
in patriotism.

And Derek,
we’ve recently uncovered the extent of firepower that the Trump
administration has given ICE to unleash on our streets. And what we were
able to uncover and expose was shocking:

[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/5891?t=1006&akid=9592%2E5257348%2EYijGb8 ]DHS dramatically increased spending to obtain weapons last year, report
says

Over the past year, the Trump administration has embarked on a mass hiring
spree to deploy ICE and CBP agents to American cities. They have also been
building heavily armed and unaccountable immigration agencies.

In just one year, ICE and CBP committed to spending more than $144 million
in taxpayer dollars on lethal firearms, ammunition, chemical weapons, and
more. This is almost a fourfold increase, in less than a year.

This is a threat to our cities and a threat to our democracy — and the
excessive and unaccountable use of force must end.

Derek, our
oversight work is just beginning and it must continue. Trump has only been
president for 13 months. There’s a lot more work to do to right his wrongs
and undo the damage he’s caused.

I won’t lie to you, this work is not easy under a Republican-controlled
Congress. Most of my colleagues in the GOP are not interested in this
oversight work, and many of them are keen on blocking it altogether.

That’s why flipping control of the House and Senate is key. That will
allow us to conduct more oversight and deliver the truth to the American
people.

I’m grateful for your support in this work,
Derek. Many Trump officials
have made me their favorite enemy — but that hasn’t stopped me before and
certainly won’t stop me now.

More soon,

Adam Schiff

We need to elect Nida and a whole new generation of leaders.

Peter,
Tomorrow is the North Carolina Democratic primary election — **and it will be the most important day in Leaders We Deserve history so far.**
In just the last few days, more than $2 million in special interest money has poured into this race to stop Nida Allam. The opposition is flooding the airwaves with attack ads because they’re scared — they know Nida has what it takes to win.
**[Before I say more, can you rush a donation of $5 to help us make sure Nida finishes strong and secures her place in Congress tomorrow?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260302_2_nida.g4gGcY&refcode=em20260302-3208&amount=5&t=2&akid=3208%2E587540%2EGvLkcT)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260302_2_nida.g4gGcY&amount=5&refcode=em20260302-3208&t=3&akid=3208%2E587540%2EGvLkcT)**
Nida is the first congressional incumbent challenger we’re backing this year. She’s taking on Rep. Valerie Foushee, an incumbent Democrat who has left working North Carolinians to suffer while she prioritizes holding onto power and stacking money from the corporations who prop her up.
**Peter, tomorrow’s race is about proving that young progressives can put up a fight. That no seat is safe when leaders refuse to be accountable to the people who elected them. And that corporate-backed politics can be challenged — and beaten.**
This election comes down to who we trust to carry our values to Washington, stand up to corporate power, and finally put working people first.
**Nida Allam is that leader.**
She’s not running because she “waited her turn.” She’s running because working families in North Carolina deserve a leader with integrity who understands the issues they’re up against — and has already delivered for her community.
If Nida wins tomorrow, it sends a message far beyond North Carolina: bold, principled leaders who are unafraid to challenge the status quo are the future of this party. Leaders who don’t just talk about their values, they put them into action.
But winning this race takes real resources. We need to counter the last-minute spending and make sure we reach every voter in the district before polls close.
**[So Peter, will you pitch in $5 to help us make sure North Carolina gets the fighter it needs in tomorrow’s primary?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260302_2_nida.g4gGcY&refcode=em20260302-3208&amount=5&t=4&akid=3208%2E587540%2EGvLkcT)**

Nida is the brighter future North Carolina deserves — and together, we can send her to Congress. Let’s leave it all on the field.
Thank you,
David Hogg

Those of us who grew up in working class communities here in Pennsylvania know at least a few people who serve in the military.
I am proud to know sailors who have served on the USS Abraham Lincoln, an aircraft carrier that is really something to see: An airport on top, two nuclear power plants in the basement, and a city of 5,000 sailors and Marines in between. Everyone has a job. Everyone has a purpose. Everyone works together.
These were the people on my mind yesterday when I heard the news that the USS Lincoln was the target of Iranian missile attacks. I also thought about their families back here at home, unable to reach their sons, daughters, sisters, brothers, and parents because the ship was in a communications lockdown. And I thought of the families of the troops who have already died or are severely wounded by the fighting this weekend.
Rep. Dan Meuser [hinted](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/cffdd3cd-ca99-4c24-a076-68a4e187257a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in an interview with WBRE this weekend that there is a good reason why we are attacking Iran and putting American lives at risk. "I know a lot about it that I can't necessarily state," he said. But to the rest of us, it's still unclear.
The American people deserve to be prepared before we go to war. That's why the role Congress plays is so important. As representatives of their communities, members of Congress can ask the hard questions.
Why now? At what risk to our troops and our allies? Is the situation with Iran so urgent that we should sacrifice American lives? What's the plan going forward?
If there is information the public doesn't know, as Meuser says, then I would look at all the facts and make a determination.
But given what we know today, I worry these decisions are not worth the loss of American lives and the threat of another unending war.
--Rachel

Peter,

**Americans spend just 8–12 seconds** on an email before deciding whether to read or delete it. I’m asking for a little more of your time today—because what’s at stake for our country couldn’t be higher.

My name is Adam Schwarze. I’m a 20+ year veteran: U.S. Marine infantryman turned Navy SEAL (Ret.), with nine deployments across more than 70 countries.

_**On September 11, 2001, I was an 18-year-old in Bloomington, Minnesota, watching the Twin Towers burn.**_ That day changed everything. I raised my right hand, swore an oath to defend this nation, and spent two decades carrying Old Glory into harm’s way—from frozen Minnesota streets to the sands of Iraq, the mountains of Afghanistan, and villages we liberated from ISIS tyranny.

I’ve watched our flag fly proudly over freed lands. I’ve seen it folded and presented to grieving Gold Star families who paid the ultimate price. **I’ve lived the cost of freedom—and I’ll never forget why we fight. But today, America feels like a different battlefield.**

**Working families can’t afford groceries while Washington elites get richer.

Our borders are wide open, fentanyl floods in, and politicians look the other way. **

**Our kids are falling behind as radical ideologies erode the values we hold dear.**

_This isn’t the America I risked my life—and lost brothers—for._

That’s why I’m running for the United States Senate in 2026. Not for a title or a career in politics. The fight didn’t end when I left the service. I don’t know how to quit, and I’m not afraid of a tough battle—just ask our enemies.

clean_body: The Clintons just defied Congress—again. | Peter, Americans spend just 8–12 seconds on an email before deciding whether to read or delete it. I’m asking for a little more of your time today—because what’s at stake for our country couldn’t be higher. My name is Adam Schwarze. I’m a 20+ year veteran: U.S. Marine infantryman turned Navy SEAL (Ret.), with nine deployments across more than 70 countries. On September 11, 2001, I was an 18-year-old in Bloomington, Minnesota, watching the Twin Towers burn. That day changed everything. I raised my right hand, swore an oath to defend this nation, and spent two decades carrying Old Glory into harm’s way—from frozen Minnesota streets to the sands of Iraq, the mountains of Afghanistan, and villages we liberated from ISIS tyranny. I’ve watched our flag fly proudly over freed lands. I’ve seen it folded and presented to grieving Gold Star families who paid the ultimate price. I’ve lived the cost of freedom—and I’ll never forget why we fight. But today, America feels like a different battlefield. Working families can’t afford groceries while Washington elites get richer. Our borders are wide open, fentanyl floods in, and politicians look the other way. Our kids are falling behind as radical ideologies erode the values we hold dear. This isn’t the America I risked my life—and lost brothers—for. That’s why I’m running for the United States Senate in 2026. Not for a title or a career in politics. The fight didn’t end when I left the service. I don’t know how to quit, and I’m not afraid of a tough battle—just ask our enemies. Minnesota’s U.S. Senate seat (held by Tina Smith) is now open for the first time in years. Republicans haven’t won it since 2008. But with strong national momentum and an energized base, this is suddenly winnable—if we build the resources to introduce my story statewide before the August primary and beyond. The problem? I’m a first-time candidate, virtually unknown to most Minnesotans outside my service record. The Democrat machine will dump tens of millions to hold this seat and push their agenda. I can’t self-fund, and I won’t back down. That’s where you come in. Together, we will: Secure the border: Welcome legal immigrants who love America; deport criminals and stop the chaos. Revive our economy: Cut wasteful spending, unleash energy independence, and restore dignity for working Minnesotans. Empower parents: Put them back in control of education, not bureaucrats or radicals. Defend the Constitution: Every word, every right—no compromises. I’ve carried our flag into the fight before. I’ve seen what it stands for. And I will never stop defending it—for Minnesota, for our kids, for a stronger, prouder America. Peter,
Mark Levin just went nuclear, and he asked a question we can no longer ignore: **
**_**"You ready, America?"**_
**Because what's happening in Texas isn't just a state issue anymore – it’s becoming Ground Zero in the battle for Western civilization.** _
_**All across Europe, countries are rapidly losing their identities as a result of unfettered mass migration with no assimilation.** **
** Parallel societies have begun to emerge and they are incompatible – one based upon Western, Judeo-Christian values, and one based upon Sharia Law, or Islamic Law.
**You could say this is just a European problem, but Sharia is the primary driver of Christian persecution across the planet, and it’s begun to gain a foothold right here in America.** **_
_** On a recent show, a retired Texas police lieutenant blew the whistle directly to Levin._**He revealed details about EPIC City – a proposed Sharia-compliant "Islamic mega-city" being planned on roughly 400 acres in Texas.** Critics claim it's designed to function separately from American society, operating under Sharia principles rather than U.S. law._ _

______**“Sharia Law has no place in the United States of America.”**____ ____**

We’re proud to support a woman like Doris, who delivers for our region, champions legislation that makes a real difference, and is rated among the most effective legislators in Congress. She authored the **Excellence in Mental Health Act,** establishing a nationwide network of Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics designed to **expand access to mental health and substance-use treatment services** across the U.S. In her role on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, she helped **craft parts of the Affordable Care Act,** and worked on legislation to lower prescription drug costs and expand **health insurance coverage.** She recently secured **$36.2 million in federal funding for Sacramento Regional Transit’s Downtown Riverfront Streetcar Connector Project,** which connects Sacramento to West Sacramento via sustainable public transit. Last year, she introduced the **Senior Savings Protection Act** to **help low-income seniors access and navigate their Medicare benefits.** When the government shutdown left families without the assistance they relied on, she **volunteered at local food banks** to help our community. She authored the Excellence in Mental Health Act, establishing a nationwide network of Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics designed to expand access to mental health and substance-use treatment services across the U.S. In her role on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, she helped craft parts of the Affordable Care Act, and worked on legislation to lower prescription drug costs and expand health insurance coverage. She recently secured $36.2 million in federal funding for Sacramento Regional Transit’s Downtown Riverfront Streetcar Connector Project, which connects Sacramento to West Sacramento via sustainable public transit. subject: Endorse the Iran War Powers Resolution
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Mark Kelly for Senate
body:
It wasn’t long ago that thousands of American families lost sons and daughters to a war with no end in sight. Trump is risking that again with Iran, and he’s doing it all without Congressional approval.
#

People who’ve never served are often the quickest to start dropping bombs without a plan for what’s next.
The American people have seen this play out before and they’re tired of it. Trump is sending our servicemembers into harm’s way without a clear explanation or end goal.
It wasn’t long ago that thousands of American families lost sons and daughters to a war with no end in sight. Trump is risking that again with Iran, and he’s doing it all without Congressional approval.
The Senate needs to come back to Washington to do its job.
I am ready to vote yes on a War Powers Resolution to prevent this from escalating any further.

This ain't the same Party that it was when I first entered the big leagues. It's become a paradise for Liberal hogwash and downright anti-American behavior.
Whether it's...

* Rioting in cities across America and burning Old Glory
* Storming ICE facilities, doxxing agents, and throwing sandwiches at law enforcement
* Having actual COMMUNISTS run some of our greatest cities

It sure seems like once you think the Democrats can't stoop any lower, they grab a shovel and prove you wrong... Guess they never heard the first rule of holes: if you're in one, STOP DIGGING.
_But let me tell you the God-honest truth. They have the money to do it and if we don 't get our act together, they just might put us in their place._
Right now, the Democrats have a well-oiled fundraising machine that is raking in the big bucks from its out-of-touch, elitist donors - 100 million bucks, to be exact.

A CBS reporter with deep connections inside the country says the message coming back is simple: Thank you, America. When you see the celebrations in Tehran and Georgetown, DC — old Iranian flags waving — you'll understand the scale of what just happened.
Mark makes the case that none of this happens without 2020, Butler, and everything in between. That argument will stick with you.

Heinrich called it "dangerously reckless." Lujan called it "illegal." Meanwhile, an Iranian-American Democrat went on CNN and said dismantling this regime is "non-negotiable" — and that she doesn't recognize her own party right now.
Then Senator Fetterman stood up. Again. The gap between him and NM's senators gets wider every week.

| | **📣 February Legislative Wrap-up** The legislature has been extremely busy since returning to the capitol. Between the House and Senate, the House filed 1,227 bills, and the Senate filed 892 bills. Today is day 50 of the 2026 legislative session. February was such a busy month for the legislature. First, this legislative session I have prime-sponsored quite a few bills, including bills to
* expand educational options (SB 1142)
* support parental rights
* secure our state's elections by requiring proof of ID in each election (SCR 1001)
* ban foreign donations in our elections (SB 1289, SCR 1013, SCR 1014)
* protect private property rights (SB 1431)
* reduce the price of small residential housing projects (SB 1241)
* uphold victims' rights (SB 1211, 1326, 1512, 1669, 1748)
* create an alternative education pathway for certified vet techs to increase our state's workforce (SB 1144)
* create a freedom of speech monument (SB 1663)
* reduce red tape for trade businesses (SB 1670)
* keep our minor children safe from social media content (SB 1747), and many more.

Second, you may have heard the Arizona democrats are trying to rollback our current school choice options and make our state's elections less secure. At the beginning of February, the democrat party filed two separate ballot initiatives potentially to be added to the November 2026 general election ballot. The education ballot measure can be found [HERE](https://bolickforarizona.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3214fdbd528e32d06cf84fc86&id=cb726fdd77&e=a7ab36849c), and their election-related constitutional amendment proposal can be found [HERE](https://bolickforarizona.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3214fdbd528e32d06cf84fc86&id=612da55235&e=a7ab36849c). If you are approaching a public library or park, walking in a parking lot, etc., please decline to sign either of these ballot proposals petitions.**📜 Bolick Bills That Passed the Senate** SB1032, SB1141, SB1142, SB1143, SB1144, SB1168, SB1289, SB1326, SB1413, SB1415, SB1431, SB1476, SB1477, SB1478, SB1586, SB1663, SB1664, SB1665, SB1670, SB1671, SB1684, SCR1001, SCR1013, and SCR1014. **🗂️ Bolick Bills Being Heard This Week in the House** SB1145, SB1210, and SB1211. **📅 What’s Next** We still have quite a few more Senate bills to vote out and send over to the House. **📺 Bolick in the News** KAWC “Arizona Senate GOP advances ballot measure to require ID for mail voting” [https://www.kawc.org/news/2026-02-18/arizona-senate-gop-advances-ballot-measure-to-require-id-for-mail-voting?_amp=true](https://bolickforarizona.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3214fdbd528e32d06cf84fc86&id=a03bceb6ca&e=a7ab36849c) Peoria Times “Senate panel advances school bullying liability bill” [https://www.peoriatimes.com/youth/senate-panel-advances-school-bullying-liability-bill/article_859585fa-dc65-4501-8b20-8cdfd3969c7a.html](https://bolickforarizona.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3214fdbd528e32d06cf84fc86&id=606a5055af&e=a7ab36849c) Fox10 Phoenix “Peoria dog seizure sparks questions surrounding strengths, limitations of Jerry’s Law” [[fox10phoenix.com]](https://bolickforarizona.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3214fdbd528e32d06cf84fc86&id=3eadc7db37&e=a7ab36849c)

subject: Judicial Watch: Records Show Unsupervised Children, False Billing, Licensing Violations at Multiple Minneapolis Daycare Facilities
body:
Judicial Watch announced that it received 458 pages of records from the Minnesota Department of Children, Youth, and Families in a Minnesota Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request that show a strong pattern of false billing, misstated attendance records, repeated licensing violations, grant fraud, and inadequate supervision of children across multiple daycare facilities in Minneapolis.

I've wanted to talk about Iran for a while, but I needed to get my thoughts together and make sure I had enough factual footing before saying anything. There is finally enough confirmed information to speak within a framework instead of speculation.
Because right now, most of the conversation is speculation.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..vatM7wEfR5Ny57YeNVHyIxSiCy0c4sfdPsoybzso3Bs?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=189699036)
Everything from "this will turn into boots on the ground" to "this will spiral into a regional war for years" to "this sparks a civil uprising and Iran becomes a democracy overnight."
On the optimistic end, people are imagining a kumbaya internal reform where the military hands power to civilians and thanks America for removing the Ayatollah. On the pessimistic end, people are predicting another Iraq or Afghanistan.
The reality is we do not know what happens next.
So let's not pretend we do. Let's talk about what we actually know.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/04c9ad01-f868-42f6-80a2-01ac01d89363?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* * *
## **The Past Is Not a Crystal Ball**
Yes, Iraq happened. Afghanistan happened. We have spent trillions of dollars over the last two decades on foreign wars and the military budget sits in the hundreds of billions to almost a trillion dollars annually.
But past outcomes do not automatically dictate future outcomes. In investing, you learn quickly that historical performance does not guarantee future results. Patterns can inform you, but they do not bind the future.
So while history should make us cautious, it should not make us intellectually lazy. History should sharpen our questions, not replace them. The strategic conditions, regional alliances, technology, intelligence capabilities, and domestic politics are not identical to 2003 .
We cannot simply say "this equals Iraq 2.0" and call it analysis.
**Now let 's talk about what we do know.**
We know that the President campaigned on no new wars. The MAGA movement and the America First message was sold as an end to forever wars. The pitch was clear: American taxpayer dollars would not be used to drag us into new foreign conflicts. No more blank checks. No more endless military entanglements.
That was the campaign.
From Venezuela regime change to Iran, from continued funding in Middle East conflicts to unilateral military action without clear congressional authorization, the results are different from the marketing.
And this is not about being naive. I am not an isolationist. Geopolitics exist. Threats exist. There are times when force may be justified.
But the American people were told one thing and they are watching another.
* * *
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..vatM7wEfR5Ny57YeNVHyIxSiCy0c4sfdPsoybzso3Bs?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=189699036)
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..vatM7wEfR5Ny57YeNVHyIxSiCy0c4sfdPsoybzso3Bs?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=189699036)
## **Congress Has Abdicated Its Role**
Another truth is that this is not just about one administration.
For years, Congress has steadily handed power to the executive branch. The Patriot Act era expanded executive authority. War powers have blurred. Major foreign policy decisions increasingly happen with minimal meaningful congressional oversight and debate. Presidents from both parties have operated with broad interpretations of authorization, and Congress has too often chosen political convenience over confrontation.
An impotent Congress that refuses to exercise its authority eventually stops having authority. When you consistently defer hard decisions to the White House or wait for the Supreme Court to resolve every major conflict, you are not governing. You are **outsourcing your job**. Over time, that becomes habit. And habit becomes structural weakness.
The American people see it. They see representatives more active on social media than on the House floor. They see hearings that generate headlines but not accountability. They see military actions initiated, funded, or sustained with little real debate and even less clarity. And they are left asking a basic question: what exactly does Congress do besides argue on television and collect a paycheck?
When military actions occur without transparent rationale, without clear objectives, without defined endpoints, and without direct congressional debate, wtf are we doing? The public is kept in the dark about intelligence assessments, strategic goals, and exit plans. Decisions feel unilateral. Information is filtered. Oversight is nonexistent.
* * *
## **The Information Environment Is a Disaster**
Here is another thing we know: trying to understand what is happening in Iran right now is extraordinarily difficult.
The amount of unreliable information circulating is astonishing. Old videos from unrelated conflicts get reposted and labeled as current events. AI-generated images and clips are passed off as firsthand footage. Anonymous accounts push dramatic claims with zero verification. Even established outlets sometimes report in real time and then walk things back hours later because the initial information was incomplete or wrong.
We hear about an American aircraft going down and within minutes there are five explanations floating at once: Iran shot it down, it was friendly fire, it was mechanical failure, it was a classified operation gone wrong, it never happened at all. You are presented with every possible narrative simultaneously and no confirmed clarity. Everything and nothing at the same time.
Trying to parse through it becomes exhausting. Even people who care deeply about policy and foreign affairs hit a wall. When every update feels like it could be false, manipulated, or emotionally engineered for engagement, skepticism turns into fatigue. Fatigue turns into apathy.
We are living in a post-truth, information-saturated environment where overload replaces understanding. And that breeds more doubt, less empathy, and less courage to take a firm position on anything. When citizens cannot confidently identify what is real, democratic accountability weakens.
That is dangerous.

[Last week I spoke at a local Democratic club about something I think we all need to take more seriously: auditing the media we consume.](https://substack.com/redirect/c7027812-4985-4912-ae84-f5600e0d8657?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* * *
## **Many Things Can Be True at the Same**
It is possible to say that the Ayatollah's regime was brutal and that tens of thousands of Iranians protesting for freedom faced horrifying repercussions.
It is possible to hope that the Iranian people get an opportunity to build a freer, more prosperous country.
It is also ok to say they should not have a nuke!
And it is also possible to ask: why are we here again?
Why are American taxpayer dollars once again funding military action overseas?
Why can we always find money for war, but struggle to fund infrastructure, healthcare, education, housing, water systems, or debt reduction?
Why does the military-industrial complex remain the one industry that never seems to face budget constraints?
Both of those thoughts can coexist.
At some point, this stops being about Iran specifically and starts being about trust.
We are tired of being sold one thing and shown another.
We are tired of campaign promises evaporating when governing gets hard.
We are tired of opaque intelligence briefings and classified rationales that the public never sees.
We are tired of being told that everything is necessary, urgent, and unavoidable.
My grandfather used to say there are two certainties in life: death and taxes.
It increasingly feels like there are three: death, taxes, and America striking another country.
That cynicism does not come from nowhere. It comes from repetition.
#### Here is what I am asking.
Do not get sucked into the speculation hype. Do not pretend you know how this ends.
Instead, go back to basics.
If a campaign was built on no new foreign wars, hold leaders accountable to that promise.
And Republicans, this applies to you first. If you believed in America First, if you believed in ending forever wars, then say it clearly. Hold your own administration accountable.
Accountability is not betrayal. It is citizenship.
We cannot keep shrugging at broken promises because it is politically inconvenient.
The American people deserve clarity, transparency, and honesty when it comes to war.
## Stay Angry.

The strategic conditions, regional alliances, technology, intelligence capabilities, and domestic politics are not identical to 2003 . We cannot simply say "this equals Iraq 2.0" and call it analysis. Now let 's talk about what we do know. We know that the President campaigned on no new wars. The MAGA movement and the America First message was sold as an end to forever wars. The pitch was clear: American taxpayer dollars would not be used to drag us into new foreign conflicts. No more blank checks. No more endless military entanglements. That was the campaign. From Venezuela regime change to Iran, from continued funding in Middle East conflicts to unilateral military action without clear congressional authorization, the results are different from the marketing. And this is not about being naive. I am not an isolationist. Geopolitics exist. Threats exist. There are times when force may be justified. But the American people were told one thing and they are watching another. Congress Has Abdicated Its Role Another truth is that this is not just about one administration. For years, Congress has steadily handed power to the executive branch. The Patriot Act era expanded executive authority. War powers have blurred. Major foreign policy decisions increasingly happen with minimal meaningful congressional oversight and debate. Presidents from both parties have operated with broad interpretations of authorization, and Congress has too often chosen political convenience over confrontation. An impotent Congress that refuses to exercise its authority eventually stops having authority. When you consistently defer hard decisions to the White House or wait for the Supreme Court to resolve every major conflict, you are not governing. You are outsourcing your job. Over time, that becomes habit. And habit becomes structural weakness. The American people see it. They see representatives more active on social media than on the House floor. They see hearings that generate headlines but not accountability. They see military actions initiated, funded, or sustained with little real debate and even less clarity. And they are left asking a basic question: what exactly does Congress do besides argue on television and collect a paycheck? When military actions occur without transparent rationale, without clear objectives, without defined endpoints, and without direct congressional debate, wtf are we doing? The public is kept in the dark about intelligence assessments, strategic goals, and exit plans. Decisions feel unilateral. Information is filtered. Oversight is nonexistent. The Information Environment Is a Disaster Here is another thing we know: trying to understand what is happening in Iran right now is extraordinarily difficult. The amount of unreliable information circulating is astonishing. Old videos from unrelated conflicts get reposted and labeled as current events. AI-generated images and clips are passed off as firsthand footage. Anonymous accounts push dramatic claims with zero verification. Even established outlets sometimes report in real time and then walk things back hours later because the initial information was incomplete or wrong. We hear about an American aircraft going down and within minutes there are five explanations floating at once: Iran shot it down, it was friendly fire, it was mechanical failure, it was a classified operation gone wrong, it never happened at all. You are presented with every possible narrative simultaneously and no confirmed clarity. Everything and nothing at the same time. Trying to parse through it becomes exhausting. Even people who care deeply about policy and foreign affairs hit a wall. When every update feels like it could be false, manipulated, or emotionally engineered for engagement, skepticism turns into fatigue. Fatigue turns into apathy. We are living in a post-truth, information-saturated environment where overload replaces understanding. And that breeds more doubt, less empathy, and less courage to take a firm position on anything. When citizens cannot confidently identify what is real, democratic accountability weakens. That is dangerous. | | | | ---|---|--- | Feb 16 | Many Things Can Be True at the Same It is possible to say that the Ayatollah's regime was brutal and that tens of thousands of Iranians protesting for freedom faced horrifying repercussions. It is possible to hope that the Iranian people get an opportunity to build a freer, more prosperous country. It is also ok to say they should not have a nuke! And it is also possible to ask: why are we here again? Why are American taxpayer dollars once again funding military action overseas? Why can we always find money for war, but struggle to fund infrastructure, healthcare, education, housing, water systems, or debt reduction? Why does the military-industrial complex remain the one industry that never seems to face budget constraints? Both of those thoughts can coexist. At some point, this stops being about Iran specifically and starts being about trust. We are tired of being sold one thing and shown another. We are tired of campaign promises evaporating when governing gets hard. We are tired of opaque intelligence briefings and classified rationales that the public never sees. We are tired of being told that everything is necessary, urgent, and unavoidable. My grandfather used to say there are two certainties in life: death and taxes. It increasingly feels like there are three: death, taxes, and America striking another country. That cynicism does not come from nowhere. It comes from repetition. Here is what I am asking. Do not get sucked into the speculation hype. Do not pretend you know how this ends. Instead, go back to basics. If a campaign was built on no new foreign wars, hold leaders accountable to that promise. And Republicans, this applies to you first. If you believed in America First, if you believed in ending forever wars, then say it clearly. Hold your own administration accountable. Accountability is not betrayal. It is citizenship. We cannot keep shrugging at broken promises because it is politically inconvenient. The American people deserve clarity, transparency, and honesty when it comes to war. Stay Angry. | Friends--
Yesterday, [HB816](https://dpxqxvhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=00148kc4P2MzQmvJTY2_ksPOfizJ9cYbxUuiiSzazldYv4Vadx4daeEFb0ZB9TWkTXpUDNs7p53BQeDgucXQH8MVic4uVqYbgmWIVWgUbopB9J-2T9PZnaCMYrZSOw_nyTiQ-_DoYgUkSRqc--M0ufcUv8CB0dR4aoKY4CP7xxZd8IUKKDPnTPRacKQGfUxH5UsSvw4ZUmNxmM5nPCidm34gjGpOodR20EgD2TpVNR5KzB-RqqyVNO1w0ZdSk3jNVpCmbSZ4ibkuI0ZpNiTfCSlNQ==&c=wMWaj0pqJxMSylovJFteRqpARbF_kSl5eFUeLsGeC7-DIQpBJO4ZEg==&ch=EtmRnC7Tn73OXYKzjNvuYV9RBvstxFSekhhRj7tIkRLKqaPYnvhMuA==), the Housing Near Jobs bill, patroned by Delegate Dan Helmer, passed the Senate Local Government committee by a bipartisan 9-6 vote. On Friday, the Senate companion, [SB454](https://dpxqxvhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=00148kc4P2MzQmvJTY2_ksPOfizJ9cYbxUuiiSzazldYv4Vadx4daeEFb0ZB9TWkTXp_9--TY0zD3qh_YVkJ_A9q7gXKTe92J1jg2JJo3ZalBs6cufwWP_Z4gnKtCAof7o6gmW6AdWV1ognvZAw1NNLKX7-zHUAVQ-XEAl8jijBdUicyqtn9vwiW2bs9Y2Da2kNOZuyJWce7M4IfrIC7GR84zJ0KGjYtTryGjM4zCwllV8hjRJQzUVgW1z6dum1c2OM5Vl9td6mwmC25_Ev-SFt8Q==&c=wMWaj0pqJxMSylovJFteRqpARbF_kSl5eFUeLsGeC7-DIQpBJO4ZEg==&ch=EtmRnC7Tn73OXYKzjNvuYV9RBvstxFSekhhRj7tIkRLKqaPYnvhMuA==), patroned by Senator Schuyler VanValkenburg, passed the House Counties, Cities, and Towns Committee by a bipartisan 11-10 vote.
The legislation would lower the cost of housing by advancing the construction of new, affordable homes in commercial zones. A [2025 YouGov poll](https://dpxqxvhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=00148kc4P2MzQmvJTY2_ksPOfizJ9cYbxUuiiSzazldYv4Vadx4daeEFb0ZB9TWkTXpKnmtwn-1M24E4A65rUpx-k8Prkh82YhU_uMra62eWtiydY7H0ICyEBdMMSzEttxkXe1mq711UXr3BGiw4L2T6fx61RLBC5vg0iJ8UsP_KpBzN7f-JMz0Q1vrJwWQ47_vQFdSnAz2A5OMo47mn1H-UVfEO4_BcpWvqF2B-bCgocbGx-Efy1fmw55gsQdHFNjC3nxZsuB5xHN5b6qZ_McKWg==&c=wMWaj0pqJxMSylovJFteRqpARbF_kSl5eFUeLsGeC7-DIQpBJO4ZEg==&ch=EtmRnC7Tn73OXYKzjNvuYV9RBvstxFSekhhRj7tIkRLKqaPYnvhMuA==) for the Commonwealth Housing Coalition found supermajority support for a variety of policies that would make it easy to build more and smaller types of homes (78%), reduce regulatory requirements on new housing (74%), require local governments to streamline home construction in Virginia (79%), empower faith congregations to build affordable housing on land they own (71%), and support local laws against severe rent hikes (77%).

name: With Honor Action
subject: General George Washington: “Every post is honorable in which a man can serve his country.” 🇺🇸
body:
On service as congressional staffers and in service to one's country.

| | | | | |
---
| | | | |
---
| | _“Every post is honorable in which a man can serve his country.” — George Washington_
---
| | Hi Peter,
Last week, With Honor Action joined the [Congressional Management Foundation](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=be9409e29f&e=33f53a5b1a) and over 100 senior Congressional staff at George Washington’s Mount Vernon, a fitting setting to reflect on character, courage, and a renewed commitment to our nation for the 250th.
With Honor Co-Founder and CEO Rye Barcott spoke about the responsibility veteran leaders bear in modeling civility, especially in Congress. He underscored that veterans bring a unique understanding of courage, not just on the battlefield, but in the halls of Congress. The courage to bridge divides, to elevate the tone of debate, and to serve a mission larger than self.
As we look toward this historic milestone, we remain steadfast in our commitment to building a Congress that leads with integrity, civility, and the courage our country deserves.
---
|
---
| |

# With Honor Action Commemorates Four Years of War in Ukraine & New Report on Defense Tech in Ukraine
---
| | On February 24, we were honored to stand alongside **Rep. Maggie Goodlander** , a Navy veteran and member of the For Country Caucus, and Ukrainian Deputy Ambassador Denys Sienik to mark four years since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Together, we reflected on the cost of this war, the resilience of the Ukrainian people, and the enduring importance of American leadership in defending freedom abroad.
---
[|
---](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=c8aa7af51b&e=33f53a5b1a)
| | We were also joined by Ukrainian soldier Andriy Smolensky, whose service and sacrifice reminded us that freedom is never free. Severely wounded in combat and now living without both his arms and his sight, Andriy delivered powerful remarks about resilience, faith, and the strength he draws from his family and his country. You can read Andriy’s story [here](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=08e11481f9&e=33f53a5b1a) and listen to his remarks below.

Today is the final opportunity to **cast your ballot** in the Primary to determine who will advance to a runoff or to the November ballot. If you care about medical liberty, parental rights, and informed consent in Texas, get in line by **7 PM TONIGHT**. If you haven’t voted yet, make a plan now and encourage others to do the same. Primary elections often come down to **small margins** , and grassroots voters decide the outcome. **But voting is only the beginning.** Between when polls close tonight and before the County/Senate District Conventions begin on March 28, local **Precinct Conventions** will be held across Texas. Most counties hold these meetings sometime this week, so check your **county GOP website** for the date, time, and location. Conventions matter. Showing up matters.**

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. subject: I’m endorsing Graham Platner
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
Graham is a Marine, like me. He’s a combat veteran. He’s lost friends, same as I have. He knows what it means to struggle, he doesn’t owe anything to the special interests, and he wakes up every day thinking about what we can do for working families.
#

Peter, it's Senator Ruben Gallego.
I’ll cut right to the chase. I’m endorsing Graham Platner for Senate in Maine to be the Democratic nominee against Susan Collins.
If that’s all you need to hear and you’re ready to join me, use this link and split a donation between me and Graham:
[**https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/platner**](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-gp.ffL9aC&refcode=em260303-1-BL&t=1&akid=4084%2E734936%2EdSTcE8)
I joined the Marines to serve my country. I watched my brothers get blown up and killed in an illegal war. When we came home we couldn’t get the help we needed from the VA. I knew, then and there, I had to do something.
I didn’t come from money. I didn’t have connections. All I had was people worth fighting for, and that ended up being enough.
Graham is a Marine, like me. He’s a combat veteran. He’s lost friends, same as I have. He knows what it means to struggle, he doesn’t owe anything to the special interests, and he wakes up every day thinking about what we can do for working families.
It’s been a long time since Maine’s had somebody like that fighting for them. Somebody that reflects their own grit and independence. If you ask me, that’s the kind of candidate that can beat Susan Collins.
We need to win in Maine to have any shot at taking back our majority in the Senate. Graham Platner can do it.
[**I’m proud to endorse Graham. And I’m asking, respectfully, if you can split a donation of $5 between his campaign and mine.**](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-gp.ffL9aC&refcode=em260303-1-BL&t=2&akid=4084%2E734936%2EdSTcE8)

# Did you know?

**Paper ballots** offer a highly secure voting method by combining physical evidence with strict oversight. Officials use **counterfeit-resistant paper** and print **enough ballots to match the total number of registered voters** , ensuring every citizen is accounted for. This is paired with **rigorous voter roll maintenance** —removing ineligible names to ensure only qualified voters participate—creating a transparent system that is easy to audit and difficult to manipulate.
---
| |
# **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**
## **_It’s official. The board is set._**
Friend,

I walked into the State Capitol yesterday, handed over my qualifying check to the Georgia GOP, and officially put my name on the May 19th primary ballot for Secretary of State.

Yes, the board is set!

When you look at the official list of announced candidates, the choice for Georgia's future is clear... crystal!

I am running against:

A **career bureaucrat** who goes on TV to defend the "status quo" while the FBI literally seizes hundreds of boxes of election records from Fulton County.

A **career legislator and former lobbyist** who thinks we can study our way out of this crisis with more committees.

A **career politician** who is running for self-identity instead of executive solutions that will create an office that truly _serves the people._

**I am the only candidate in this race who has actually signed the front of a paycheck.**

Georgia does not need another bureaucrat, lobbyist nor politician taking up space in the Secretary of State's office. We need a complete, top-to-bottom corporate turnaround.

As your next Secretary of State, I am bringing Day 1 "Administrative Readiness" to this broken and poorly led agency. That means prosecuting illegal voters, ending the Dominion contract, eliminating QR Codes and moving to secure hand-marked paper ballots, cleaning the voter rolls, and creating a customer service-focused Licensing Division so we stop treating Georgia's job creators like a government nuisance.

We have the momentum, but the establishment is about to pour everything they have into stopping a true conservative CEO and former Air Force Officer from cleaning up their mess.

**I have set a strict 48-Hour "Official Qualifier" fundraising goal of $10,000 to immediately fund our digital strike team and get our turnaround plan in front of every high-information voter in this state.**

body:
Good Work, Good People, Good Week
| | | | | | [ ](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01KJSZ5B93PFJZ23T2VZ158MAX_0)
---
| **Welcome to the Barlow for Wyoming Newsletter. Your hub for latest news, information and upcoming events.**
---
|
---
| | |
---
| Good Work, Good People, Good Week
---
| Hi friends,
This past week at the Capitol was a good one, with lots of great conversations and progress. The Stem Cell Freedom Act passed both chambers without a single 'no' vote and is headed for signature later this week. I am thrilled we can offer this progress for people who need options. Our Senate Joint Resolution to Protect Public Lands and Keep Decisions Local is still in the House, where the discussion continues. Protecting access and keeping decisions rooted in Wyoming communities remains important work. The state budget was passed yesterday, with both sides reaching an agreement on a 2-year budget of just under 10 billion dollars. The budget will go to the Governor next, where he can take actions, including line-item vetoes. There were long days and steady work, and I appreciate the colleagues on both sides of the Legislature who rolled up their sleeves to get it done for Wyoming. Outside the chamber, we stayed busy as well. Kelly came to town with 4H and joined me to attend the Hearts for Hunger Breakfast, Leap Into Leadership dinner with Nina and Nini McConigly, and the Governor’s Prayer Breakfast, which are always uplifting. I hosted tours for students from Campbell County and Thunder Basin High Schools, and the Heritage Christian School, all from Gillette. We attended the Governor's Arts Awards Reception, and finished the weekend with a meet-and-greet in Saratoga, a great legislative update with Sen. Gary Crum in Laramie and the UW Men's Basketball Game, where the Cowboys beat Air Force. Always good to see that scoreboard. As the session winds down, we’re turning our focus back to the campaign trail. We’ll be getting back out across the state in the weeks and months ahead, spending time in communities and hearing what's important to Wyomingites. You can keep an eye on the schedule posted here and on our Facebook page for upcoming events. I’m looking forward to seeing more of you around Wyoming soon.
---
|
---
| | | IN THE NEWS WYOMING NEWS NOW [Barlow for Wyoming Governor on-air segment](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01KJSZ5B93PFJZ23T2VZ158MAX_1) GILLETTE NEWS RECORD [Stem Cell Freedom Act passes House and Senate without a single 'no' vote](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01KJSZ5B93PFJZ23T2VZ158MAX_2) “This is your cells, for your body, for your healing. Period.” KOTA News [Wyoming legislature passes Stem Cell Freedom Act, giving access to unapproved treatments](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01KJSZ5B93PFJZ23T2VZ158MAX_3) “What we’re saying is that the speed of science is faster than the speed of bureaucracy,” Barlow said. “The scientific community is learning things about the power of healing of our human cells and the regulatory framework that we have in the federal government just does not keep up.” COWBOY STATE DAILY [The Stem Cell Freedom Act: Your Stem Cells, For Your Treatment](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01KJSZ5B93PFJZ23T2VZ158MAX_4) “For too many patients, the federal system moves far slower than illness or injury,”

| | | AROUND THE CAPITOL Hearts for Hunger Breakfast Our hearts were full at the Hearts for Hunger Breakfast with First Lady Jennie Gordon and the Wyoming Hunger Initiative this morning. Kelly and our daughter Kate joined me. Governor's Art Awards Good to see familiar faces from around the state, including Dan and Lynn Kirkbride and Beth Worthen at the Governor's Art Awards. Congratulations to awardees:
Community Fine Arts Center, Rock Springs Becky Larsen, Lander Ernie Marsh, Lovell Susan Miller, Sheridan

---

| | | Leadership at the Capitol I was able to meet with groups attending leadership events while they were at the Capitol last week, including Leap into Leadership, Leadership Cheyenne, and the Wyoming 4H State Leadership Team. The Leadership Cheyenne and 4-H State Leadership groups took a tour of the Capitol, during which I shared some information about the history and processes we see most days of the session. (top photo and right). Grateful for the opportunity to spend the day with the Wyoming State Leadership Team for 4-H Civics Day. It’s always inspiring to see young leaders engaged, informed, and committed to making a difference in their communities. Thank you to those across the state who are working together to make their communities better.

# FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
---
|
### What's happening on Friday night?
Candidates and organizations host events throughout the city the night before the Convention. Delegates & Guests enjoy these lively social events! There will also be a chance to pick up your credentials at a pre-registration event hosted at the AC Marriott. Many decide to spend the night on Friday.
View our hotel blocks here: [https://massgop.com/massgop-convention-2026-hotels/](https://qgzxgy5ab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018-mfCmmhvobnTL5vzv9BPNSpyyGe542GyIkjQXe0OoEm8V8pN0o7bK3mc7wFz-F8p2shH8q5EspeMfhzclDvVob5Q91I6mOJp9f6QhlUOGEqKTBW6hlZXgUvjEtayvem6ymkaLsFLfulAexJQQmsrTxa-lcVzeoCYa_uwL84fDHND98gTq9MfMdXuAby0Hj5dW8YxUL5Rs8=&c=59MytgOTcL1eYCo-jHvQKUvI9QKRa-r2mSH5UmyqXhvvRgqabewNww==&ch=6266ifQnbG2FiA4VHpVmYpew8IXqpgGgeKCM6EWpshwXguxcS2Zp5w==)

### How long should I plan to be at the Convention on Saturday?
Convention is a full day affair, plan to be there for a full business day. Right now, that means you should plan to be in the building from 9a-5pm.

### Who will speak from the national scene?
At least one guest speaker has been confirmed, with additional speakers still in the process of being finalized! Past speakers include Congressman Byron Donalds (R-Florida) and Tom Homan.

### Will there be a vendor hall?
Yes. MassGOP State Committeeman Chris Ryan has been appointed as the vendor manager - [Geolopes@comcast.net](mailto:Geolopes@comcast.net).
You can expect Media & Candidate Tables, Private Vendors and Non-Profits to be located inside the Convention building but outside of the arena.

### Will there be food & beverage available?
Yes, the DCU Concession stands will be open and operating.

### Will there be assigned seats?
Town & City Ward Committees have assigned seating areas. Delegates will be directed where to find the location of their committee after check-in.

### What is the dress code?
Dress code is business, but this is a convention, so expect a wide range from suits to American flags head to toe. Have fun with it and dress comfortably!

### Can guests go?
Yes! Guest passes are available at [https://secure.winred.com/massachusetts-gop/2026guestfee](https://qgzxgy5ab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018-mfCmmhvobnTL5vzv9BPNSpyyGe542GyIkjQXe0OoEm8V8pN0o7bMIZiPogXfyQ5C2xYjVM_QFnsSUpzNiET1rmzCVixQzqbUy7IWncDJyEhQh1aj08rso6mgH6piizK6WilXYMvrdD69dExpLFBntTxS3ZAliLP_f6V2xqhUq7C_6zveF8Zwv8A3ngBtJV1rx3zI9KU08=&c=59MytgOTcL1eYCo-jHvQKUvI9QKRa-r2mSH5UmyqXhvvRgqabewNww==&ch=6266ifQnbG2FiA4VHpVmYpew8IXqpgGgeKCM6EWpshwXguxcS2Zp5w==) Guests must pay a fee and do not vote or have access to Committee seating areas.
Who should I contact if I have questions? Your State Committee Members are your best resource for all things Convention.
A list of members is available by district on the MassGOP website here: [https://massgop.com/our-party/committee/](https://qgzxgy5ab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018-mfCmmhvobnTL5vzv9BPNSpyyGe542GyIkjQXe0OoEm8V8pN0o7bF8lS4t5dcz7Y0PpxZv7RncvuuU9gTqDbLUeql8uWGq-xws-JW23s29CruoK8SA6OQeIY1r8cBZ6y7VJfvzJUuSV4usJaUgDs4w5YAKSuqPsavLb0cBAN9MTUNBWTDQP2Q==&c=59MytgOTcL1eYCo-jHvQKUvI9QKRa-r2mSH5UmyqXhvvRgqabewNww==&ch=6266ifQnbG2FiA4VHpVmYpew8IXqpgGgeKCM6EWpshwXguxcS2Zp5w==)
For questions about delegate report submissions, please contact MassGOP's Political Director Aidan Carey at [aidan@massgop.com](mailto:aidan@massgop.com).

[This is a longer email, but I respectfully ask you to read it start to finish.](https://links.trueamericanconservatives.com/s/c/QLte1RUaIv71LV9ZKJiXrPrlOdF7tAf_Y8Cw9LA6nDVmpHeYpX6EKytaOg9mOikRzEUfW4bAAbULY4A_XD3SVBoEZZarlcWg_hKQcJ9MukpPSNnNhTGWHM9kizMC8e0bEJdbdEWyV2n_DIonmjk2kULdpZTQ0TqqiuiRK2jG3TTlI5syqvWFYuWdfO60kVUWQBbGX8I1U6uS3zizSwo1zK4EhIoJxY9o4CQHf0gL3RoIJYFidSrRszyH5ge0UQ2vEdRk0UZJ4eO2pVngF6kcUnputXid4SgOWaEvmtH6OmPxD4hCkN0qrGzSSMTCADXmT2xXYZlsUcDzQkGWx3doqVtvmNUt10V08vT0MQMWgytOpxrclA8h6Jv_mvqLdQWtT8XIklSd6ljQNsmwlXPctexxy3SK4_sqnFupi1qvwIvo4gsQULqrJFXLjNg4dGtHm8Kt1m8eK--f2jU8HN2EcDLnVY3KIl-CrZ3pdmrY_qqAhCL6QjY8ETHNXpTTbSWT8gh4sf0X32KimYiMHBijisR-Kxh0UQyHd-hc3yyskvmrbeeuMrGNSdjniaSAsJJJlnTqwxZAI5-rdQiJeCqgCV4I9KqcjuxmOu2k4V6CacFlnbHILJBiS57oqTmpmq3d124NraZ94XuBfo1OaR9m8HqOxCj-KPihc2WaW8D0NH_lDyqtS00gsIpV7MWM_hwblKxHOtbDlEITZOj382d9C4vblQvtPIdEJ5kbk6kjr9f-hrtzzV8lHIGmHo1-XjmvoMDp/6aR8SgwQLo7TnEEpTkeq71T6TkI3WpY2/18)
It wasn't easy telling the world I grew up dirt poor, I was raised by my Mamaw while my mother struggled with addiction.
It wasn't exactly the prep school/trust fund/summer-in-the-Hamptons upbringing that is commonplace in DC.
But I felt God called me to tell my story. Warts and all. I felt led to speak out because I believe millions of Americans share stories like mine. Stories of jobs being outsourced to China, addiction ravaging communities and killing our neighbors, and heeding the call of duty after the Towers fell on 9/11.
As your Vice President, I now stand in the breach for the left-behind, forgotten men and women who built this country, but were abandoned by the political class in DC.
I'll do everything in my power to make sure that never happens again. I'll fight every day for good folks like you.
I promise to always stand between you and the Democrat Machine that aims to obliterate everything that makes our country great.
[Which brings me to the purpose of my email today.](https://links.trueamericanconservatives.com/s/c/8K9VLHjChuMUEjJ8iMzXU-i-7w7SY54hL59StkTjINZjKpIGvQRak6tVf29PRgmI3OSin1gLxFwv0GXEgDc8-lv4a2uZzRnE7t78N1jI3bngCD_XRHNZ9WU7cPziJoM1NI2iUdBTLp7gxK6BSzanNQdzw1qUbLCoz9heLrMF4ZRSylGGb7BBfYkESXmWG75VOL6gG9ouOEzTu757p2ycOeb6CBjjcRJlxjJ48UXpPiAMQbcVi98E0Tzz02b45u-WqJHB0LuT9fFcu3eXvDVfAzJqfCvPtm3oHH9-xDnnAhDkCWw7KBDfMPaCfBN370YVxBg7JsBE_3ug8GfOlpi7TBiFTnVbVBWJX7HJWPj8euFv_RTqJhWFze8uYGon514cfpwO39aXhD7f1-2Wf0p_GQp63Q5WP8hFKu39zaSJTojQ6zTuael6RxCEcJDSSy3HpoEfl6__stpadYdMPqzXTg3aIi202l3hBVZGtBb2-jfO1dBig_mD16peNbmd0XJm40ywLR2qeNq-aKW6lCOM-5OrF6x9pZJPLfyXM3Y1_bwiYqjsrGQ_tlJ6POQ4r9PScz10aYgvr3F-Ef2OxOsB-4XXoSVvKaoXTedL4D7GMoqk2tZC5PMWlgEiSaFQ9n9tyr2vTcsQYq37XJ4p7ctRD6w66jFh-yMj3OxpgPlF0sfY8mlfE0fmeDJ3bSKZXI8cHemV3ySX58WF7nlTdQemvVyx5qTDs6AzcbGrXwjmNGntEeKIOlRbhm-WK38q87-nZpMB/0Jhl1ambuC3TCO2CsJVykE7_7-6QiIkt/18)
We're coming out of the most expensive election in American history. I mean that. Kamala Harris spent over a billion dollars against us. It took EVERY PENNY we had to get our story out there, expose her ultra-Liberal record, reach undecided voters, and win.
So now we're forced to rebuild.
The Democrat Machine is ALREADY crushing us in fundraising, ALREADY outspending us in key races, and ALREADY building the campaign infrastructure to decimate us in the Midterm Elections.
At this point, the consequences of simply resting on our laurels would be unthinkable.
So here's my final pitch to you:
[I’m teaming up with Majority Leader Steve Scalise to raise a million dollars by the end of the month.](https://links.trueamericanconservatives.com/s/c/yhNIANyn1EicgwRyXVZJBKGO6hqjyus4L9BGk-jkPCxpWs0K38_gCzDXEmQhixS4oVuOMKgNC-m-Nj2M49IAx7S9aTw-wKnb4JH4ZdSdLgjmhvh4T1iAH6XfPx4yytZiC2Rer4PLATWjXLufud3FzmLdN-SK9rwyeGecPKEuD1bArqzGOVvzzjav1XEs-I9cUgFqJVWw8499_00jbc-3ziakQISBv3xDJ4Uc4k6_mcQlHKJzJc6X8-S8PRXXgQVLnXjhpoquvjAcX4NUlCFbcgjsBAcb3kzK24zpfbZdL0Oy_wPe_FW9ER7RB3T6YMcswwv0QhDDeOk1LEkmI2cge60WYQlW1_XD23KZOY7OIgLqseaxIh4BZ-KUy2BWrOxwNJU9RmNfaUbBWXR1pJJj7oVvW-n0VnPzLXtSiMY3WoF_B-OfbdSTy2TbhrfBCeNEeuVys0Lb0qWC1IxoJFGeWh5DSOimo17Uf9dS-sjyOUMTFomUc0G8WYpQLXnCXmLmzMvbIZbUIOfXwx-XxCYji5TPSE-DvgMkYoknyrJbRtqUkA1VvN2JVEZIUesTEdkJA1nCw8OTR1u4kKFKcmFAykAzq1Xw4dvg0p5ObX1xfrmOiRfrdmNxHZqltyQx7wpEr9KdRCZoWyVX-31f7pSnNfGfQhYX36A_dnLWd-AJ6YyzaKruTFS-x5LU-GRvrHeNHVeeINPPmnICQFRUasGrnCKlafNdaeQs5WmST1ynrS8BjeElE-7-dr1Mf3nOuS1i7B9u/mXIibmEdH_U4l_Y_2k0C6zljKmh2XYwX/18) I understand that's ambitious. But if that's what it takes to deliver President Trump a Republican House for his entire second term, it's a no-brainer. I'll do what it takes to win.

Peter, We are at a crossroads. As the current administration pushes an agenda that many experts warn mirrors the early warning signs of authoritarianism, we cannot afford to look away. To fight back, we must first recognize the tactics being used to dismantle our democracy. Today, we begin a new series on the **14 Signs of Fascism** , starting with the first and most visible: **Powerful and Continuing Nationalism.** In a healthy democracy, patriotism is a quiet love of country and community. The experts use fancy words like "Singularity" to describe this, but it comes down to a simple reality: the world is running out of cheap silver.

# **Austin bar shooter had history of Islamic extremism, hate toward conservative women and antisemitism**
Ndiaga Diagne, the 53-year-old Senegalese national killed by police Sunday **[after shooting three people dead and wounding over a dozen at an Austin bar,](https://substack.com/redirect/2b98fa04-42ad-490c-971f-b6d4123d4cc7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** had a history of spewing hateful messages online, including calling conservative women "whores," praising the Islamic revolution as "eternal," and hurling antisemitic and racist remarks routinely flagged as "hateful conduct" on X.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2b98fa04-42ad-490c-971f-b6d4123d4cc7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Ndiaga Diagne
* **Why it matters:** Diagne was wearing a "Property of Allah" sweatshirt over a shirt bearing the Iranian flag during the attack, and a Quran was recovered from his car. Authorities believe he may have been motivated by US and Israeli missile strikes on Iran that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. The FBI and local police are investigating the attack as a potential act of terrorism.
* **What he posted:** Diagne wrote "the Islamic revolution is eternal and here to stay until the end of time" in an April 2025 post, telling "Zionist and islamophobes" they "can't do a damn thing about it." He viciously attacked conservative figures including Laura Loomer ("shut the f--k up you Israel first wh--e, move to Israel you f--king bitch") and congressional candidate Valentina Gomez ("you ain't one of them wet back bitch"). He also called Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu "evil" and told Ivanka Trump after she praised her father's Middle East peace push that "they think they can turn GAZA into a real estate development" and "the atrocities of the settlers occupying Palestine will come to an end."

* * *
# **Jasmine Crockett responds to Islamic terror attack in Texas bar by saying most shooters are "white"**
Neither of the two Democratic frontrunners in Texas' Senate primary--James Talarico and Rep. Jasmine Crockett--addressed concerns about Islamic terrorism after a deadly Austin shooting Sunday left three dead and over a dozen wounded, instead focusing on gun control and warning against stereotyping immigrants. Talarico called for "universal background checks" and "red flag laws," while **[Crockett claimed that the majority of shooters"have been white." ](https://substack.com/redirect/3ccb7284-4f52-43c0-80fe-4be7b8386ce9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* **Crockett 's words:** "If I was to give you the facts as to who the shooters have been in these mass shootings, I can guarantee you -- the vast majority of them have been White, male and homegrown. But we don't see them taking any action on that," Crockett said.

* **GOP response:** RNC spokesman Zach Kraft condemned the Democrats' response as "absolutely disgusting," saying they're "blaming hardworking Texans who go to church and lawfully own guns, instead of the radical Islamic terrorist." Texas Republicans blamed the shooting on Biden's border policies, with Rep. Wesley Hunt saying "this is what happened when you had four years of an open border" and 20 million illegal entries, calling the shooter an "animal."

# **Female American pilot smiles at Kuwaiti rescuers after being accidentally shot down during Iran strikes**
An American F-15 pilot **[appeared to be grinning and standing easily](https://substack.com/redirect/1c3746a2-4cec-417b-8cbe-75febb11d6f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after ejecting from her jet when it was accidentally shot down by Kuwaiti air defenses Sunday during US assaults on Iran, according to purported viral footage. The pilot confirmed she was OK to rescuers, who said "thank you for helping us," prompting her to raise her hands as if to say "you're welcome."

This is Dennis Price. I'm a Marine Special operator and private military contractor with over 15 deployments who now leads rescue operations, humanitarian and medical aid – all led by the Holy Spirit “to free the oppressed, so others may live.” **Since 2022, I've been the founder and leader of Heroes for Humanity – a network of special operators, veterans, first responders, medical professionals, and everyday people committed to being the hands and feet of Jesus.** We were born in the chaos of Afghanistan's fall in 2021 – where I personally helped evacuate 77 Americans and vetted Afghan allies, even swimming the Panjshir River behind enemy lines to pull people out. And just the other day, we rescued 8 families from the chaos and violence in Mexico. But our story goes much deeper than even that.
---
---

## Under the Gold Dome
---
| Here are the bills we're watching closely this session to make sure our elections remain secure, taxpayer dollars are responsibly used, and our freedoms are safeguarded.
AFY 26 Budget - Passed and Sent to Governor
* HB 973 - Includes income and property tax relief, transportation investments, funding for the Georgia DREAMS Scholarship endowment, and mental and rural healthcare investments (Sponsor: Jon Burns)

Election Integrity
* SB 568 and SB 214 -- Both seek to address compliance with removing QR codes from Georgia ballots (Sponsor of 568: Greg Dolezal, Sponsor of 214: Max Burns)
* HB 215 (Voter Integrity Act) \-- Prohibits state election officials from remaining in the Electronic Registration Information Center, or ERIC, and sharing voter registration data with non-governmental entities. (Sponsor: Martin Momtahan)
* HB 963 \-- Prohibits foreign nationals from contributing to or participating in any campaign (Sponsor: Chuck Martin)

Affordability
* HB 1001 - Reduces the state individual income tax rate to 4.99%. (Sponsor: Will Wade)
* HB 1063 - Protects residential and small business customers from costs tied to large data center energy usage. (Sponsor: Brad Thomas)
* SB 392 (Waste Reduction Act) - Applies zero-based budgeting principles to increase transparency and review departmental spending. (Sponsor: John Albers)

Children & Education
* HB 1193 - Advances statewide early literacy and reading initiatives. (Sponsor: Chris Erwin)
* SB 433 (Rio's Law) - Authorizes special license plates for individuals with autism or developmental disabilities and their families. (Sponsor: Brian Strickland)
* SB 513 - Addresses chronic absenteeism by establishing clearer consequences for repeated unexcused absences. (Sponsor: Jason Dickerson)
* HB 1009 - Restricts personal electronic device use during the school day for grades 9-12\. (Sponsor: Scott Hilton)

Insurance Affordability and Accountability
* HB 1262 - Increases penalties for violations of Georgia insurance law, including mental health parity and surprise billing. (Sponsor: Eddie Lumsden)
* HB 1274 - Allows the Insurance Commissioner to order refunds of excess insurer profits under certain conditions. (Sponsor: Matt Reeves)
* HB 1344 - Strengthens enforcement authority and oversight related to insurance fraud, rates, and claims processing. (Sponsor: Matt Reeves)
